1. **[blocking][issue-impact] F1 — The non-Unix startup path still drops and re-binds the selected port.** [`spawn_with_listener`](crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:226) drops the owned listener before spawning the child, explicitly relying on `jit-server` to bind `--bind` again. This violates REQ-2’s “no code path re-binds” requirement and retains the race on supported non-Unix builds.

2. **[blocking][issue-impact] F2 — Unix handoff fails when the parent environment already has `LISTEN_PID`.** [`inherit_listener`](crates/jit/src/commands/serve.rs:194) sets `LISTEN_FDS` but does not remove inherited `LISTEN_PID`, despite documenting that it must be unset. The child then declines the inherited descriptor and falls back to the second bind in [`resolve_listener`](crates/server/src/lib.rs:45); because the parent still holds the socket, startup fails. Existing tests scrub the environment before exercising the path, so they do not cover this case.

Total findings: 2

findings.summary: The listener handoff still violates REQ-2 on non-Unix and when an inherited LISTEN_PID prevents Unix descriptor adoption.
